terms.meaning: Quantisation that uses the largest absolute value in a tensor or group to determine a scale.
Declining to supply an answer when sufficient evidence is unavailable.
The fraction of evaluated examples counted as correct.
Adaptive discriminator augmentation: adjust data augmentation to reduce discriminator overfitting.
Small added weights trained while the base is fixed.
Making corresponding representations or outputs agree; in this week's multimodal setting, matching content across modalities.
An interface through which one program asks another to do work.
A service providing programmatic access to models, typically with authentication, quotas, monitoring and billing.
A numbered position used to select an item or a matrix row.
Automatic speech recognition: turning speech audio into text.
One set of query, key and value projections and its weighted information mixture.
Rules marking which token pairs an attention operation may use; Boolean conventions vary by API.
An encoder-decoder network trained to reconstruct its input through an intermediate representation.
Generate a next token from the input and previously generated tokens.
Processing several inputs together in one model operation.
Decoding that retains a fixed number of high-scoring partial sequences as candidates at each step.
Two neighbouring symbols; this model predicts from the previous character only.
Predicting between two labels, here real and generated.
A reference-overlap measure using modified n-gram precision and a brevity penalty, originally developed for translation.
A keyword-ranking method based on term matches and their frequency.
A technical standard for signed content-provenance records; valid credentials establish recorded claims, not the truth of depicted events.
Stored results reused when an equivalent request returns.
Losing previously learned capabilities when training adapts a model to new data or tasks.
A model predicting the next token from the tokens already present.
A rule preventing a position from attending to later positions.
Intermediate reasoning steps generated before a final answer; written reasoning can be incorrect or unfaithful to internal computation.
Caption hallucination assessment with image relevance: measures mentions of objects unsupported by an image's annotated content.
Model-specific formatting used to represent roles and messages as a token sequence.
A passage cut from a document for indexing and retrieval.
Verbatim segment equality against the particular cited passage; it does not establish complete sentences, entailment or source truth.
A similarity between image and text representations; it is not a complete quality measure.
A measurement including specified initialisation work; state which downloads or setup it includes.
Balancing model size and training data to minimise loss under a fixed compute budget; the balance depends on the experiment.
The probability of an outcome when some other information is already given.
Evaluation data appearing in training or tuning data, which can make measured performance misleading.
The input text made available to a language model for a response.
Choosing and arranging instructions, examples, evidence and tool results within a model's available context.
The maximum sequence length a model can process in one call; input and generated output can share this budget.
Serving requests in batches whose membership can change between generation steps as requests arrive and finish.
Learning representations by making matched examples more similar than unmatched examples under a chosen objective.
An added conditioning network that guides diffusion generation using structural inputs such as edges, depth or pose.
A comparison of vector directions, independent of vector length.
A learned unrestricted score, used instead of a probability-valued discriminator.
Attention whose queries come from one representation and whose keys and values come from another.
The average negative log-probability assigned to outcomes under a target distribution; one-hot targets give negative log-likelihood.
Relating information from different data modalities, such as an image and its caption.
Alpha-bar at time t: the product of one minus each earlier noise variance β; it controls the retained signal term.
Denoising diffusion implicit model: a sampler using selected noise levels; its usual η=0 setting is deterministic given starting noise.
Denoising diffusion probabilistic model: a learned reverse process that generates data from noise, usually through stochastic updates.
A network that turns a representation or previous outputs into predictions for the output.
Selecting and generating output tokens using the model's predictions and a chosen generation procedure.
Synthetic or manipulated media made to convincingly depict a person or event in a way that can mislead.
The learned network; here it predicts added noise from noisy data and a timestep.
Rank passages by similarity between learned question and passage vectors.
Keep tensor values while disconnecting their gradient path for an operation.
Generation through learned denoising of a noisy representation.
A transformer denoiser that processes image or latent patches together with noise-level and conditioning information.
A model that predicts a label or target from an input without modelling the input distribution.
A network trained to distinguish dataset examples from generated examples.
Training a student model to imitate a teacher's outputs or behaviour, often to reduce computation.
A packaged filesystem and configuration used to create application containers with their dependencies.
Direct preference optimisation: train on preferred and rejected responses using a reference-relative loss, without a separate reward-model training stage or online RL loop.
Separate encoders for two input types whose representations are compared using a similarity function.
An image-to-image setting controlling how much the input is perturbed before denoising.
A lower bound on data log-likelihood; its negative balances reconstruction and KL at β = 1.
Exponential moving average: a weighted average of recent model weights.
A numerical vector representing an item, often learned, for prediction or comparison.
A network that converts input data into numerical representations or distribution parameters.
A URL and request handler through which a program exposes an operation.
One pass through the training data.
Code that runs examples, scores outputs and collects comparable measures.
Retrying with progressively longer waits, often increasing geometrically and adding random jitter.
A Python framework for implementing HTTP APIs with typed request handling and validation.
A numerical representation extracted from an intermediate layer of a network.
A small neural network applied separately at each token position.
A prompt containing several examples of the desired input/output behaviour.
Learning a velocity field from targets defined along selected paths between distributions; generation integrates that learned field.
A fixed procedure that progressively corrupts clean data with noise.
A model trained on broad data that can be adapted to a range of downstream tasks.
A model weight held unchanged by the optimizer during training.
Updating all model weights during adaptation to new data or a task.
A named piece of code taking inputs and returning an output.
Random numerical values drawn from a bell-shaped distribution.
A model of how data is distributed, used to sample new examples, optionally given a condition.
How much generated data lies in the real-data region of a chosen feature space.
How much real-data variety is covered by generated data in a chosen feature space.
A network that transforms a random code into a generated example.
A measure of how changing a quantity would change a loss.
A training cost encouraging the critic's input-gradient norm to stay near one on sampled interpolates.
A Python library for building interactive interfaces around models or other functions.
A reference answer or observation used to check a model output.
Quantisation using separate scales, and sometimes offsets, for groups of values instead of one scale for all values.
Group relative policy optimisation: a reinforcement-learning method that estimates relative advantages from a group of sampled answers.
A rule or check that constrains inputs, outputs or actions; it can reduce risk but is not a guarantee of correctness.
Combining conditional and reference predictions to influence prompt-following during sampling.
Generated content that presents an unsupported or incorrect claim as if it were reliable.
The response used here when request validation fails before generation.
An HTTP response indicating too many requests; retries should respect the service's instructions and a bounded attempt budget.
A numerical array holding a batch of images, their channels, rows, and columns.
Generating an edited image from an input image and a condition, often by adding noise and denoising with a new prompt.
Performing a task using information or examples in the prompt without updating model weights.
An instruction planted in retrieved data that tries to redirect the assistant.
Using a trained model to predict or generate without updating its learned weights.
A contrastive negative-log-probability objective that distinguishes a matching example from negative examples using normalised similarity scores.
Generating content within a selected region of an image while conditioning on the surrounding content.
A message carrying application or system instructions; its role and priority depend on the model or API contract.
Supervised fine-tuning on examples presented as instructions and desired responses across tasks.
A category describing what a customer's message is asking about.
An attempt to make a model bypass its intended safety or instruction constraints.
A structured text format for exchanging fields and values, including objects and lists.
Kernel inception distance: compare real and generated feature distributions using a kernel statistic.
A non-negative measure of how one probability distribution differs from another.
The elapsed time from a request to its result; first-token latency measures the initial wait.
A shorter hidden numerical representation used by the model.
Generating in a compact image representation before a decoder converts it to pixels.
Following a path between latent codes and decoding intermediate points to inspect how outputs change.
The space of hidden codes used by a model; VAE training encourages their distribution to resemble a prior.
An unobserved variable used to explain observed data; a generative model may sample it before decoding.
The advantage gained by falsely dismissing authentic evidence as fabricated when convincing synthetic media is possible.
The probability or density assigned to observed data, considered as a function of model parameters.
Using a language model to score outputs against a rubric; validate its agreement, biases and reliability.
An unnormalised model score. Sigmoid or softmax can turn logits into probabilities.
Code that repeats a task for several items or steps.
Small trainable matrices adding a low-rank correction to selected base-model projections.
A number measuring prediction error during training.
Multiplying a vector by learned weights to produce another vector.
The number of rows and columns in a table of numbers.
Choosing model parameters to maximise the likelihood of the observed training data.
A protocol through which applications discover and call tools and access resources.
The centre of a distribution and a measure of its spread.
The average of human ratings on a specified quality scale; report the scale, raters and evaluation conditions.
The average squared difference between predicted and target numbers.
A type of data, such as text, images or audio, with its own structure.
A separation between representation distributions for different modalities, even within a nominally shared embedding space.
A generator produces only a small part of the variety present in the training distribution.
Documentation describing a model's intended uses, evaluation, limitations, training information and licence.
A learned number used by a neural network to transform its input.
Mean reciprocal rank: average one over each first relevant result's rank; missing results score zero.
Combining information from different modalities, at input features, intermediate layers or output decisions.
A language model system that processes, and sometimes generates, multiple data modalities alongside text.
A count-based model that predicts the next symbol using the preceding n minus one symbols.
Trained jointly on sequences containing multiple modalities, rather than only attaching a separately trained input converter.
A score measuring how surprising observed data is; lower is better for those data.
A reference text condition used by some guidance methods to steer generation away from specified content.
Learned numbers used to transform an input into a prediction.
A network's estimate of the noise added to a representation at a specified noise level.
Numbers specifying how much signal and noise appear at each timestep.
The generator objective that asks D to label generated samples as real.
The leading token candidates retained by a top-p cumulative-probability threshold.
A prompt that includes one worked input-output example of the task.
A model with downloadable trained weights; its licence determines permitted use and does not necessarily provide training data.
An endpoint implementing a specified part of an OpenAI request-response format; supported routes and behaviours can differ.
Generating additional content beyond an image's original boundaries.
Learning training examples in a way that fails to improve predictions on separate examples.
A latency value at or below which roughly 95% of measured requests fall.
vLLM's attention approach that manages key-value-cache storage in paged blocks to reduce memory fragmentation.
Two examples marked as describing the same content.
Returned relevant passage IDs divided by all independently labelled relevant passage IDs.
A projection that compresses vectors into fewer dimensions for inspection.
Application control deciding whether a proposed operation may execute.
The exponential of average negative log-probability, summarising prediction uncertainty.
A disclosed fixed local decision route, separate from model planning.
Polling-based object-hallucination evaluation that tests whether a vision-language model incorrectly claims objects are present.
A judge's preference for an answer's placement rather than its quality.
Further training after pre-training to adapt capabilities or behaviour, such as instruction or preference tuning.
A failure where the decoder largely ignores the latent code and the inferred code distribution approaches the prior.
Proximal policy optimisation: a reinforcement-learning method that limits policy changes during reward-based updates; it is used in some RLHF pipelines.
Initial training on broad data, often using targets constructed from the data itself.
The fraction of the k returned results that are relevant.
Processing prompt tokens to initialise a model's generation state, often including its key-value cache.
Reusing stored computation for an identical prompt prefix when the model and relevant settings permit it.
Learning continuous prefix representations, often attention keys and values at several layers, while keeping the base model fixed.
The chosen code distribution used for generating new examples, here N(0, I).
A number from 0 to 1 describing how likely an outcome is.
A rule assigning probabilities to outcomes; discrete probability masses sum to one, while continuous densities integrate to one.
A learned mapping connecting feature dimensions or representation spaces.
Instructions and context supplied to a model for one request.
Passing results through a sequence of prompts, each handling a defined part of a task.
Instructions inside supplied content that attempt to redirect the model's task.
Learning continuous input vectors while keeping the main model weights fixed.
Information about a media item's origin and editing history.
Training low-rank adapters through a frozen, typically 4-bit quantised base model to reduce fine-tuning memory.
Representing weights with a limited set of values, often to store fewer bits.
Learned vectors used to compare tokens and mix their information.
The adapter's intermediate feature dimension, controlling its correction capacity and parameter count.
A service-imposed cap on requests, tokens or other usage within a time interval; limits depend on the service and account.
A model that reorders candidate passages by reading them with the question.
A model trained to use additional intermediate computation before answering; that computation does not guarantee correctness.
A flow-based generative approach that learns velocity targets along straight paired paths; learned sampling trajectories need not be straight.
Learning to predict numerical values rather than selecting a class label.
Writing a random code as learned shift and scale applied to independent noise.
Adding a sublayer's output to the vector entering that sublayer.
Saved complete answers reused only when all response-changing inputs match.
The learned sampling process that moves a noisy representation towards data through successive denoising updates.
Increasing a measured reward by exploiting its weaknesses while failing the intended task.
A model trained to score outputs from feedback, such as human comparisons; its score approximates the desired preference.
Reinforcement learning from human feedback: optimise a model using rewards derived from human judgements; a reward model and PPO are one implementation.
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, using outcomes that can be checked, such as tests or known answers.
Assigning a role in a prompt to influence the model's style or task framing; it does not confer expertise.
A family of reference-overlap measures often used for summarisation, including n-gram and longest-subsequence variants.
Reciprocal rank fusion: combine rankings using candidates' rank positions.
The procedure that uses model predictions to turn starting noise into an output.
Drawing an outcome randomly according to a probability distribution.
An empirical relationship describing how quantities such as loss change with model size, data or compute.
A specification of output fields, types and allowed values.
The gradient of log probability density with respect to the input; Gaussian diffusion connects it to scaled noise prediction.
Sampling several reasoning paths and aggregating their final answers, often by majority vote.
A vector space where corresponding inputs from different modalities can be compared.
A score comparing two representations; larger means more similar here.
A comparatively compact language model; no universal parameter threshold defines the term.
Turns a row of scores into nonnegative numbers summing to one.
A time-frequency representation showing the strength of frequency components in an audio signal over time.
A draft model proposes output tokens and a target model verifies them; the acceptance rule determines distribution preservation.
An output constrained to a specified structure or schema; valid structure does not guarantee correct content.
Learning from supplied input prompts and known desired responses.
Producing answers that agree with a user's stated view despite conflicting evidence or a better-supported answer.
Invented requests used to exercise an application and its monitoring.
Google DeepMind's family of watermarking methods for identifying supported types of AI-generated content.
A positive divisor on model scores that changes how concentrated sampling probabilities are.
An array whose axes name groups such as batch, token position and feature.
The number of entries along each dimension of an array.
Computation spent during inference, such as longer reasoning, repeated sampling or search, rather than during training.
An in-process HTTP request tester; its timing excludes real network transport.
Work completed per unit time, such as total generated tokens per second.
A unit processed or generated by a model; a text token can be a word, word part or character.
An integer identifying a text unit in one particular tokenizer's vocabulary.
Output-token count divided by a stated time interval; specify whether the interval covers decoding or the whole request.
A named function application code can run for the model.
A structured request for the program to run a named function.
Sampling after retaining only the k highest-probability token candidates and renormalising their probabilities.
Recording linked operations in a request so their timings, dependencies and failures can be inspected.
Separate examples for learning, choosing settings and final measurement.
Separate examples for learning and for the final, fair check.
Learning a model's parameters or probability table from data.
A number used to measure mistakes and guide weight updates.
The known answer used to measure a model's prediction error.
Time to first token; this lab approximates it with first non-empty decoded text.
Text-to-speech: turning written words into an audio waveform.
Two time-scale update rule: separate learning rates for the generator and discriminator.
An image network with shrinking and expanding spatial stages joined by skip connections.
An ordered list of numbers used to represent an item.
Fine-tuning a vision-language model on image-conditioned instructions and desired answers or conversations.
Producing an answer to a question using information from an image.
Vector representations of image patches or features supplied to a language model; they need not be discrete text-token IDs.
A vision-language model that processes images together with text.
Generating speech that imitates a speaker's voice from reference audio; assess consent and misuse risks.
A vector-quantised autoencoder that represents inputs using entries from a learned discrete codebook.
A measurement after specified initialisation or warm-up; state what work it excludes.
A signal embedded in content to support later identification; detection can be imperfect or altered by transformations.
Word substitutions, deletions and insertions divided by reference word count.
A prompt describing the task without including worked input/output examples.
Select a class by comparing descriptions, without training on that task's labels.
A variational autoencoder with a multiplier β on its KL penalty, changing the reconstruction-regularisation tradeoff.
